method: Bit error rate is the probability that a detected bit is wrong on a coherent receiver fed by an additive white Gaussian noise channel with no coding. BPSK and QPSK each carry one coded bit per dimension and give Pb = Q(sqrt(2 Eb/N0)); Gray-coded 8-PSK gives Pb = (2/3) Q(sqrt(6 Eb/N0) sin(pi/8)); square M-QAM gives Pb = (4/k)(1 - 1/sqrt(M)) Q(sqrt(3k Eb/N0/(M-1))) with k = log2 M, which is 0.75 Q(sqrt(0.8 Eb/N0)) for 16-QAM and (7/12) Q(sqrt(2 Eb/N0/7)) for 64-QAM. The Gaussian tail Q(x) is evaluated as erfc(x/sqrt(2))/2, and erfc is computed as the regularized incomplete gamma function Q(1/2, x^2) through its series and continued-fraction expansions, so small error rates keep their relative accuracy instead of cancelling against 1. The Eb/N0 needed for a target rate is found by 200 bisection steps on the same curve between -10 and 60 dB; an entry that cannot reach the target inside that window is reported as outside the range. Margin is the entered Eb/N0 minus that requirement, and Es/N0 is Eb/N0 + 10 log10(k) for a noise bandwidth equal to the symbol rate. These are the standard Gray-coded approximations, accurate to within a fraction of a decibel at practical error rates but not exact symbol-error expressions; unequal constellations, fading, interference, phase noise, synchronisation loss, equalisation, channel coding and hardware impairments are not modelled, so results are planning and teaching estimates rather than link certification. It stores, uploads and transmits nothing and runs entirely in the browser.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Bit error rate: coherent BPSK and QPSK over an AWGN channel give a bit error probability of Q(sqrt(2 Eb/N0)), with Eb/N0 the energy per bit over the one-sided noise power spectral density.
Wikipedia, Phase-shift keying: the Gray-coded symbol error probability for M-PSK is approximated by 2 Q(sqrt(2 log2 M Eb/N0) sin(pi/M)), which gives the 2/3 factor for bits of 8-PSK.
Wikipedia, Quadrature amplitude modulation: square M-QAM with Gray coding has the bit error approximation (4/log2 M)(1 - 1/sqrt(M)) Q(sqrt(3 log2 M Eb/N0/(M-1))).

Abramowitz and Stegun, Handbook of Mathematical Functions: the complementary error function equals the regularized upper incomplete gamma function Q(1/2, x^2), and the Gaussian tail follows as erfc(x/sqrt2)/2.
Proakis, Digital Communications: these Gaussian-tail expressions are the standard uncoded coherent detection results used to size a link margin for a target bit error rate.
